Ostrander Mackerel.narrative: I crew on Ostrander Cormorant's boat and I mean to have a net and a boat of my own before I am thirty. My mother Sella Pike the elder keeps a fried-fish stall by the tide steps and fed me on credit for years; my sister Sella Mackerel cooks at the fish market and is the better hand with a pan of anyone on the quay. I am courting Sella Tallow, and her father Bramwell wants a fisher with a boat, not a crewman with a net still to buy, so every tide I put by what I can. The wall is not built and the stone stays dear, and I fear the sea will take the lower quay again before the quay folk ever agree on it.
values: the quay's wall built before the next surge
goals: save enough marks for a net of my own
prove to Bramwell Tallow I am worth his daughter
clear what I owe Ilse Ostrander for a winter's suppers

memories.gist: The night the Surge came, I carried my mother's stall pots up the steps and watched the lower quay go under.
My first full season crewing for Ostrander Cormorant, and the first coin I ever put by toward a net.
Sella Tallow laughed at my landing and shared her fried fish with me on the tide steps, and I have been courting her since.
Ilse Ostrander fed me suppers all one lean winter and told me to pay when I had a boat.
The carters came down the fish road saying the stone from Kettlebridge would cost more again, and the quay folk cursed.

stances.why: Bramwell Tallow will not give me Sella without one, and I would not ask him to.
Ilse fed me when I had nothing; a debt like that is paid, not forgotten.
If the sea takes the lower quay again there will be no stalls to rebuild.
Kettlebridge sells us stone dear and the quay goes unbuilt for it.
Ostrander Cormorant knows the deep water and I mean to learn it off him.

Sella Mackerel.narrative: I cook at the fish market and keep a stall of fried fish and bread, and I mean to have that stall rebuilt in stone before the next surge takes it. My mother Sella Pike the elder has fed the quay on credit for years and taught me the pan; my brother Ostrander Mackerel crews on Ostrander Cormorant's boat and is courting Sella Tallow, and I hear both sides of the quay's quarrels while I fry. The Warden will not hear of building until the seawall is paid for, and I think the rebuild would bring trade enough to pay for the wall twice over. I hear Marrow Wrack and Gideon Fenwick each call the other a cheat, and I think the quarrel keeps good stone out of the quay.
values: good fried fish and fair prices
keeping the stall's marks in my own apron
goals: keep her brother from overreaching on credit
get the Warden to listen about the rebuild
Sella Mackerel.mood: busy and impatient with the Warden

relations.name: Jory Pike

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay and my mother's stall with it; we fried fish on the upper steps for a month after.
I fried my first fish at my mother's stall and sold the whole batch before the morning boats came in.
Ostrander Mackerel told me he meant to court Sella Tallow, and I told him to save for the net first.
I heard Marrow Wrack and Gideon Fenwick each call the other a cheat over a load of brick, and the carters took sides.
Ostrander Vane patched the lower quay with salvage timber and I thought, that should be stone, and said so.

stances.why: Timber went under in the Surge; stone would not have.
A working lower quay would pay for the wall twice over, and the Warden will not see it.
My mother fed the quay on credit and got little back; I keep the stall's marks in my own apron.
Wrack and Fenwick each call the other a cheat and the good stone stays in Kettlebridge for it.
He would owe the whole quay for a net; someone in the family should count.
